title: Ethiopia and Eritrea Cut Ties as Fighting Grows in the North
summary:
Two neighboring countries in Africa, Ethiopia and Eritrea, have just cut their diplomatic ties. That means they are pulling their ambassadors and closing their embassies — the offices where countries talk to each other.

On Thursday, Ethiopia said it was closing its embassy in Eritrea's capital, Asmara. It ordered 10 Eritrean diplomats to leave Ethiopia within 48 hours. Ethiopia accused them of activities that threatened national security. Eritrea said it had no choice but to cut all ties in return. Its foreign ministry called Ethiopia's decision "astounding."

The split comes as heavy fighting has returned to northern Ethiopia. More than 50 people have been killed since last week. Ethiopian forces are battling fighters from the Tigray People's Liberation Front and its allies in the regions of Tigray, Afar and Amhara.

This is a big change. In 2018, Ethiopia's leader, Abiy Ahmed, restored peace with Eritrea after 20 years of hostility. That earned him the Nobel Peace Prize in 2019. Now relations have fallen apart again. Ethiopia also told an Egyptian diplomat to leave. The government did not say why.
why_it_matters: When countries stop talking to each other, problems get harder to fix, and ordinary people — including kids — can lose their homes and schools, just like the families who fled northern Ethiopia.

background_read: Ethiopia and Eritrea (two neighbouring countries in the Horn of Africa, the eastern part of the continent) fought a long and deadly border war that ended in 2000, and for about 20 years they would barely talk to each other.
In 2018 Ethiopia's leader Abiy Ahmed made peace with Eritrea, and that peace won him the Nobel Peace Prize in 2019 — an award given in Norway each year to people who work for peace.

The Tigray People's Liberation Front is a political and armed group from Ethiopia's northern Tigray region; when it fought Ethiopia's government, the fighting spread to nearby regions and many families had to leave their homes.

WHAT: Ethiopia closed its embassy in Asmara and ordered 10 Eritrean diplomats out, so Eritrea cut all ties in return.
WHERE: The two countries' capitals and embassies, and the northern Ethiopian regions of Tigray, Afar and Amhara.
WHY: Ethiopia accused the diplomats of threatening national security, and heavy fighting has returned to the north, killing more than 50 people since last week.

perspectives.description: It says the Eritrean diplomats were doing things that threatened Ethiopia's national security, so they had to be sent away.
Eritrea's foreign ministry called Ethiopia's decision 'astounding' and said it had no choice but to cut all ties in return.
Observers point out this is a huge reversal: only a few years ago the two countries ended 20 years of hostility and Abiy Ahmed won the Nobel Peace Prize for it.
